content.json:
## AI Control Tower (Feature 23)

Cost, quality and health for every AI call this application makes, **on one shared time axis** —
a cost spike, a quality drop and an alert firing on the same day line up vertically, they are not
three things you have to notice separately. Every chart below is day-over-day, not a point-in-time
snapshot.

**Data sources, and what is live today (checked 2026-08-21):**

| Section | Source | Live now? |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Cost | `customEvents` / `llm_agent_call` (Feature 23 Phase 1) | **No — empty.** `customEvents` has 0 rows over the last 90 days because `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` is not yet set as a Container App secret on `invoice-be` / `queue-worker`. Phase 1 emits to stdout only until it is. |
| 2. Quality | `customEvents` / `agent_eval_run` (Feature 23 Phase 3) | **No — empty**, same reason, plus the nightly eval job is not scheduled yet. The durable copy of these rows is the Postgres `agent_eval_run` table, which a workbook cannot query (workbook data sources are Logs / ARG / ARM / ADX — not Postgres); `scripts/run_agent_eval.py` therefore writes the row *and* emits this event. |
| 2. Cost by tool | `customEvents` / `llm_agent_call`, `sage.*` agent names only | **No — empty**, and doubly so: `ENABLE_AGENTIC_SAGE` is off, so no `sage.*` event will appear even after the connection string is set. |
| 3. Latency | `customEvents` / `llm_agent_call` | **No — empty**, same connection-string reason. |
| 5. Component quality | `customEvents` / `agent_eval_run`, `context_score` / `orchestration_score` / `persona_score` | **No — empty.** The columns and the scorers exist (`services/agent_eval.py`, migration `c4a91e77b208`); nothing has run against a live tenant. |
| 6. Online signals | `customEvents` / `online_eval_signal` | **No — nothing emits them yet.** `services/online_eval_signals.py` computes all five over Postgres and `emit_online_signals()` mirrors them as events, but no scheduled job calls it. Empty here means "nothing has run", **not** "no problems found". |
| 7. Golden-bank coverage | Static figure from `tests/golden_bank/golden_bank.json` | **Yes, but not live.** A workbook cannot read a repo file; the numbers in that section are from a real run and are dated. |
| 8. Health | Azure Resource Graph `alertsmanagementresources` | **Yes.** Verified live against this subscription. |

**Cost rates are an assumption.** `$/1M tokens` per model is hardcoded in the two cost queries below
(gpt-5-mini $0.25 in / $2.00 out as of 2026-08-21) and must be re-checked against the Azure OpenAI
pricing page for this deployment's region before any figure here is treated as real money. A model
with no rate shows a blank cost, never a zero.

parameters.name: Tenant
parameters.label: Tenant
parameters.query:
customEvents
| where name in ('llm_agent_call', 'agent_eval_run')
| extend tenant_id = tostring(customDimensions['tenant_id'])
| where isnotempty(tenant_id)
| distinct tenant_id
| order by tenant_id asc

### 1. Cost — day over day

USD per day per agent, from real token counts. `eval.*` agents are this feature's own judge calls; they are inside the totals by design and split out in the table below.

content.query:
let rates = datatable(model:string, usd_per_1m_in:real, usd_per_1m_out:real)["gpt-5-mini",0.25,2.00,"gpt-5",1.25,10.00,"gpt-4o-mini",0.15,0.60,"gpt-4o",2.50,10.00,"mock",0.0,0.0];
customEvents
| where name == 'llm_agent_call'
| extend agent_name = tostring(customDimensions['agent_name']),
         model = tostring(customDimensions['model']),
         tenant_id = tostring(customDimensions['tenant_id']),
         tokens_in = toint(customDimensions['tokens_in']),
         tokens_out = toint(customDimensions['tokens_out'])
| where '{Tenant}' == 'all' or tenant_id == '{Tenant}'
| lookup kind=leftouter rates on model
| extend cost_usd = (tokens_in * usd_per_1m_in + tokens_out * usd_per_1m_out) / 1000000.0
| summarize cost_usd = sum(cost_usd) by bin(timestamp, 1d), agent_name
| render timechart
content.title: Model spend per day, by agent (USD)

let rates = datatable(model:string, usd_per_1m_in:real, usd_per_1m_out:real)["gpt-5-mini",0.25,2.00,"gpt-5",1.25,10.00,"gpt-4o-mini",0.15,0.60,"gpt-4o",2.50,10.00,"mock",0.0,0.0];
customEvents
| where name == 'llm_agent_call'
| extend agent_name = tostring(customDimensions['agent_name']),
         model = tostring(customDimensions['model']),
         tenant_id = tostring(customDimensions['tenant_id']),
         status = tostring(customDimensions['status']),
         tokens_in = toint(customDimensions['tokens_in']),
         tokens_out = toint(customDimensions['tokens_out']),
         latency_ms = todouble(customDimensions['latency_ms'])
| where '{Tenant}' == 'all' or tenant_id == '{Tenant}'
| summarize calls = count(), errors = countif(status == 'error'),
            tokens_in = sum(tokens_in), tokens_out = sum(tokens_out),
            p95_latency_ms = percentile(latency_ms, 95)
  by day = startofday(timestamp), agent_name, model
| lookup kind=leftouter rates on model
| extend cost_usd = iff(isnull(usd_per_1m_in), real(null),
         (tokens_in * usd_per_1m_in + tokens_out * usd_per_1m_out) / 1000000.0)
| extend spend_kind = iff(agent_name startswith 'eval.', 'evaluation', 'product')
| project day, spend_kind, agent_name, model, calls, errors, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd, p95_latency_ms
| order by day desc, cost_usd desc
content.title: Spend, calls, errors and p95 latency by day / agent / model

content.json:
### 2. Cost by tool — where a SAGE turn's tokens actually go

The full breakdown and its caveats live in `infra/monitoring/llm_cost_by_tool.kql`. The one thing to know before reading these two panels:

**`get_full_record` has no event of its own, and that is not an instrumentation gap.** It makes no LLM call — it reads the ORM row and `get_all_invoice_chunks()`, and the planner puts every chunk it returns into the *next* `sage.synthesis` prompt. So the full-chunk dump's cost is not missing from telemetry, it is inside `sage.synthesis`'s `tokens_in` and nowhere else. `synthesis_share_pct` in the second panel is therefore the answer to "what does the chunk dump cost relative to the rest of the turn" — by inference from prompt size rather than by direct measurement. The direct measurement exists only offline, in `scripts/run_agent_eval.py`'s `tool_calls[].chunk_tokens`, where the `large_invoice_full_detail` / `small_invoice_full_detail` pair isolates it exactly (same question, same tool path, 11 indexed pages against 1).

The five instrumented SAGE call sites, read off the code rather than assumed: `sage.planner` and `sage.synthesis` (`agents/sage_orchestrator.py`), `sage.identify`, `sage.aggregate` and `sage.search` (`agents/query_tools.py`).

content.query:
let rates = datatable(model:string, usd_per_1m_in:real, usd_per_1m_out:real)["gpt-5-mini",0.25,2.00,"gpt-5",1.25,10.00,"gpt-4o-mini",0.15,0.60,"gpt-4o",2.50,10.00,"mock",0.0,0.0];
let calls = customEvents
| where name == 'llm_agent_call'
| extend agent_name = tostring(customDimensions['agent_name']),
         model = tostring(customDimensions['model']),
         tenant_id = tostring(customDimensions['tenant_id']),
         request_id = tostring(customDimensions['request_id']),
         status = tostring(customDimensions['status']),
         tokens_in = toint(customDimensions['tokens_in']),
         tokens_out = toint(customDimensions['tokens_out']),
         latency_ms = todouble(customDimensions['latency_ms'])
| where '{Tenant}' == 'all' or tenant_id == '{Tenant}'
| lookup kind=leftouter rates on model
| extend cost_usd = (tokens_in * usd_per_1m_in + tokens_out * usd_per_1m_out) / 1000000.0;
let by_agent = calls
| where agent_name startswith 'sage.'
| summarize calls = count(), errors = countif(status == 'error'),
            tokens_in = sum(tokens_in), tokens_out = sum(tokens_out),
            cost_usd = sum(cost_usd), p95_latency_ms = percentile(latency_ms, 95)
  by day = startofday(timestamp), agent_name;
let day_totals = by_agent
| summarize sage_tokens_in = sum(tokens_in), sage_cost_usd = sum(cost_usd) by day;
by_agent
| join kind=leftouter day_totals on day
| extend share_of_sage_tokens_pct = round(100.0 * tokens_in / sage_tokens_in, 1),
         share_of_sage_cost_pct = round(100.0 * cost_usd / sage_cost_usd, 1),
         avg_tokens_in_per_call = round(1.0 * tokens_in / calls, 0)
| project day, agent_name, calls, errors, tokens_in, avg_tokens_in_per_call,
          share_of_sage_tokens_pct, tokens_out, cost_usd, share_of_sage_cost_pct, p95_latency_ms
| order by day desc, cost_usd desc
content.title: Cost and tokens per SAGE tool-level agent, per day

content.json:
### 3. Latency — day over day, its own panel

Median **and** p95 per agent per day, as separate series. Deliberately not folded into the cost table: a p95 column beside a cost column reads as a footnote, and latency regression is its own failure mode with its own history here — Gap 278 was two ~177s chat turns with **zero** 4xx/5xx, which no error-rate chart and no cost chart would ever have shown. Both percentiles are plotted because the gap between them is the signal: a median that holds while the p95 climbs is a tail problem, and a tail problem is what a user reports as "chat is broken sometimes".

Scope note: this measures **one LLM round-trip**, not one chat turn. A turn is several calls plus queue wait, and no per-turn latency is recorded anywhere in the product (see section 6's `slow_turn_rate` caveat). The only real per-turn figure today is the offline harness's, in the Postgres `agent_eval_run.latency_ms` column and on the quality event.

content.query:
let latencies = customEvents
| where name == 'llm_agent_call'
| extend agent_name = tostring(customDimensions['agent_name']),
         tenant_id = tostring(customDimensions['tenant_id']),
         status = tostring(customDimensions['status']),
         latency_ms = todouble(customDimensions['latency_ms'])
| where '{Tenant}' == 'all' or tenant_id == '{Tenant}';
let binned = latencies
| summarize p50 = percentile(latency_ms, 50), p95 = percentile(latency_ms, 95)
  by bin(timestamp, 1d), agent_name;
union
  (binned | project timestamp, series = strcat(agent_name, ' p50'), latency_ms = p50),
  (binned | project timestamp, series = strcat(agent_name, ' p95'), latency_ms = p95)
| render timechart
content.title: Median and p95 latency per day, by agent (ms)

         latency_ms = todouble(customDimensions['latency_ms'])

latencies

            p50_ms = percentile(latency_ms, 50), p95_ms = percentile(latency_ms, 95),
            p99_ms = percentile(latency_ms, 99), max_ms = max(latency_ms)

### 4. Quality — day over day

The golden sample re-asked on a schedule and graded on faithfulness / relevance / accuracy (`services/agent_eval.py`). A drop here on the same day as a cost spike above is the pattern this workbook exists to make visible.

content.query:
customEvents
| where name == 'agent_eval_run'
| extend agent_name = tostring(customDimensions['agent_name']),
         tenant_id = tostring(customDimensions['tenant_id']),
         passed = toint(customDimensions['pass']),
         faithfulness = todouble(customDimensions['faithfulness_score']),
         relevance = todouble(customDimensions['relevance_score']),
         accuracy = todouble(customDimensions['accuracy_score'])
| where '{Tenant}' == 'all' or tenant_id == '{Tenant}'
| summarize pass_rate = avg(passed), faithfulness = avg(faithfulness),
            relevance = avg(relevance), accuracy = avg(accuracy)
  by bin(timestamp, 1d), agent_name
| render timechart
content.title: Pass rate and mean scores per day, by agent

content.json:
### 5. Component-level quality — which stage of the pipeline is wrong

Three separate trend lines, never one average — the mean of a retrieval score and a tax-reasoning score is not a quantity. Section 4 above says *that* an answer was bad; this section says *which part to fix*:

| Component | What it isolates | How it is scored |
|---|---|---|
| **context** | Did retrieval fetch the right underlying rows, independent of how the model reasoned over them | **Deterministic.** F1 of fetched invoice ids against the golden case's known-correct set. No LLM judge, no judge variance, no marginal cost. A case whose correct retrieval is *nothing* scores 1.0 for fetching nothing — Gap 224's shape, and the most diagnostic case in the set. |
| **orchestration** | Given whatever was fetched, did the answer stay inside it | **Mechanical.** Every figure in the answer must appear in a tool result, or be one arithmetic operation over two of them (a `compute()` output). Score = traceable / total. Also no judge. Small bare integers (<100, no decimal) are skipped rather than graded, and the skipped count is reported. |
| **persona** | Given correct data and correct instruction-following, was the *domain* reasoning right — tax components, RCM, status semantics, category judgement | **LLM-judged.** The one component that genuinely needs judgement rather than checking. |

**Read `persona_scored_turns` before reading `persona`.** There is no dedicated domain-knowledge golden set in this repo — checked, not assumed: the 9-case sample and the 87-case seeded bank are both general tenant-regression questions with no domain-reasoning axis. Rather than block the component on authoring a new bank, the judge scores the general sample against a persona-focused rubric and returns *not applicable* for every turn that required no domain judgement — which is most of them. So the persona line is a signal about a small, self-selected subset, not a coverage measure of domain competence. Writing that bank is still outstanding.

None of the three feeds the pass/fail decision. Folding them in would redefine what a pass means halfway through the series, which is the one thing a trend must not do.

content.query:
let evals = customEvents
| where name == 'agent_eval_run'
| extend agent_name = tostring(customDimensions['agent_name']),
         case_id = tostring(customDimensions['case_id']),
         tenant_id = tostring(customDimensions['tenant_id']),
         context_score = todouble(customDimensions['context_score']),
         orchestration_score = todouble(customDimensions['orchestration_score']),
         persona_score = todouble(customDimensions['persona_score'])
| where '{Tenant}' == 'all' or tenant_id == '{Tenant}';
let binned = evals
| summarize context = avg(context_score), orchestration = avg(orchestration_score),
            persona = avg(persona_score)
  by bin(timestamp, 1d), agent_name;
union
  (binned | project timestamp, component = strcat(agent_name, ' context'), score = context),
  (binned | project timestamp, component = strcat(agent_name, ' orchestration'), score = orchestration),
  (binned | project timestamp, component = strcat(agent_name, ' persona'), score = persona)
| where isnotnull(score)
| render timechart
content.title: Context / orchestration / persona per day, as three separate lines

content.query:

content.query:
let evals = customEvents
| where name == 'agent_eval_run'
| extend agent_name = tostring(customDimensions['agent_name']),
         case_id = tostring(customDimensions['case_id']),
         tenant_id = tostring(customDimensions['tenant_id']),
         context_score = todouble(customDimensions['context_score']),
         orchestration_score = todouble(customDimensions['orchestration_score']),
         persona_score = todouble(customDimensions['persona_score'])
| where '{Tenant}' == 'all' or tenant_id == '{Tenant}';
evals
| summarize arg_max(timestamp, context_score, orchestration_score, persona_score)
  by day = startofday(timestamp), agent_name, case_id
| extend worst = min_of(coalesce(context_score, 1.0), coalesce(orchestration_score, 1.0), coalesce(persona_score, 1.0))

    persona_score < 0.8, 'right data, correctly cited, wrong domain reasoning',

| project day, agent_name, case_id, context_score, orchestration_score, persona_score, worst, diagnosis
| order by day desc, worst asc
content.title: Worst component per case per day — the diagnosis, not just the score

content.json:
### 6. Online signals — live traffic, no ground truth

The five shapes `services/online_eval_signals.py` computes over `chat_message` / `chat_feedback` / `agent_eval_run`, mirrored here as `online_eval_signal` custom events by `emit_online_signals()` because a workbook cannot query Postgres. Every one of the five is a shape this repo actually hit, not a hypothetical.

**These signals are not equally solid, and the panel says so on every row** — `confidence` travels on the event itself, it is not a footnote in a doc somewhere:

| Signal | Confidence | What it really measures | Default alert |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zero_result_rate` | **measured** | `chat_message.content` containing the product's own `NO_RECORDS_FOUND` constant. Gap 224's *false-confident-zero* sub-shape (a confident `USD 0.00` with no "no records found" anywhere) is counted separately — rolling the two together would make a fleet of correct refusals look like a fleet of fabrications. | 20% |
| `thumbs_down_clustering` | **measured** | `chat_feedback` votes, clustered by day/session/reason/tenant. The clusters are the signal; the rate is only context for them, because `ChatFeedback` records what someone chose to vote on, not overall quality. | 20% rate **or** any cluster ≥ 3 |
| `slow_turn_rate` | **proxy** | **`ChatMessage` has no duration column and there is no per-turn timer anywhere in the product.** This is the assistant row's `created_at` minus its own user row's — a row-timestamp delta, not a measurement. Under Gap 280's queue path that delta is genuinely end-to-end (user row written at enqueue, assistant row after the agent returns, so it includes queue wait, which is what the user experiences), but it carries clock-skew and retry caveats, and negative deltas are discarded rather than clamped. An authoritative number needs a latency column on `ChatMessage` or the Phase 1 telemetry event. | 5% over 45s |
| `budget_exhaustion_rate` | **offline-only** | **No live turn persists a `stop_reason`.** `agents/sage_orchestrator.py` computes `tool_call_budget_exhausted` / `clarification_requested` / `planner_step_budget_exhausted` and `run_agentic_sage()` returns them in metadata, but `ChatMessage` has no column for them and nothing writes them anywhere durable. The only persisted copy in the repo is the free-text `agent_eval_run.notes` written by `scripts/run_agent_eval.py` — so this measures the **eval harness**, not production, and it is parsed out of prose rather than read from a column. Closing it needs a `stop_reason` column on `ChatMessage`, or the Trace-level capture. | 10% |
| `clarification_rate` | **heuristic** | `ask_clarifying_question()` returns the question verbatim as the turn's answer with no marker of any kind (`sage_orchestrator._clarify_node`), so there is nothing in the row to match on but the wording. Additionally the SAGE path that produces most clarifications is behind `ENABLE_AGENTIC_SAGE`, which is off — a near-zero live rate today is a configuration fact, not a quality result. | 25% |

Two reading rules built into the module and preserved here: **no signal alerts below 20 observations** (1-of-1 is 100%, the commonest way a quality dashboard cries wolf), and a **blank `value` always means "nothing to measure", never 0.0** — an empty window must not read as a healthy one.

**Nothing emits these events yet.** No scheduled job, ACA cron or request path calls `emit_online_signals()`. An empty panel here means "nothing has run", not "no problems found".

content.query:
let signals = customEvents
| where name == 'online_eval_signal'
| extend signal_name = tostring(customDimensions['signal_name']),
         tenant_id = tostring(customDimensions['tenant_id']),
         confidence = tostring(customDimensions['confidence']),
         value = todouble(customDimensions['value']),
         threshold = todouble(customDimensions['threshold']),
         numerator = toint(customDimensions['numerator']),
         denominator = toint(customDimensions['denominator']),
         breached = toint(customDimensions['breached']),
         false_confident_zero_turns = toint(customDimensions['false_confident_zero_turns']),
         cluster_count = toint(customDimensions['cluster_count']),
         p50_seconds = todouble(customDimensions['p50_seconds']),
         p95_seconds = todouble(customDimensions['p95_seconds'])
| where '{Tenant}' == 'all' or tenant_id == '{Tenant}';
signals
| where isnotnull(value)
| summarize rate = avg(value) by bin(timestamp, 1d), signal_name
| render timechart
content.title: Signal rates per day (a gap in a line is 'not measured', not zero)

let signals = customEvents
| where name == 'online_eval_signal'
| extend signal_name = tostring(customDimensions['signal_name']),
         tenant_id = tostring(customDimensions['tenant_id']),
         confidence = tostring(customDimensions['confidence']),
         value = todouble(customDimensions['value']),
         threshold = todouble(customDimensions['threshold']),
         numerator = toint(customDimensions['numerator']),
         denominator = toint(customDimensions['denominator']),
         breached = toint(customDimensions['breached']),
         false_confident_zero_turns = toint(customDimensions['false_confident_zero_turns']),
         cluster_count = toint(customDimensions['cluster_count']),
         p50_seconds = todouble(customDimensions['p50_seconds']),
         p95_seconds = todouble(customDimensions['p95_seconds'])
| where '{Tenant}' == 'all' or tenant_id == '{Tenant}';
signals
| summarize arg_max(timestamp, value, confidence, threshold, numerator, denominator,
                    breached, false_confident_zero_turns, cluster_count, p50_seconds, p95_seconds)
  by signal_name
| extend trustworthy_sample = denominator >= 20
| project timestamp, signal_name, confidence, value, threshold, breached,
          numerator, denominator, trustworthy_sample,
          false_confident_zero_turns, cluster_count, p50_seconds, p95_seconds
| order by breached desc, signal_name asc
content.title: Latest reading per signal, with its confidence and its denominator

         p95_seconds = todouble(customDimensions['p95_seconds'])
| where '{Tenant}' == 'all' or tenant_id == '{Tenant}';
signals
| where signal_name == 'slow_turn_rate'
| where isnotnull(p50_seconds) or isnotnull(p95_seconds)
| summarize p50_seconds = avg(p50_seconds), p95_seconds = avg(p95_seconds),
            slow_turns = sum(numerator), turns = sum(denominator)
  by day = startofday(timestamp)
| extend slow_turn_rate = round(1.0 * slow_turns / turns, 3)
| order by day desc

content.json:
### 7. Golden-bank coverage — how much of the gap history is actually re-runnable

**A static figure, not a live query.** A workbook has no data source that can read a repo file; these numbers come from `tests/golden_bank/golden_bank.json`'s own `gap_coverage` block, generated by a real run of `scripts/seed_golden_bank.py` and **re-verified against that file on 2026-08-21** (fixture `generated_at` 2026-08-21T14:16:40Z). Regenerate with `uv run python scripts/seed_golden_bank.py` and update this block; if it ever disagrees with the fixture, the fixture is right.

| Gap coverage | Count |
|---|---|
| Gap entries in `be_features_tracker.md` | 182 |
| Closed (`[x]`) | 177 |
| Closed **answer-quality** gaps (strict: the gap's own title is about chat / answers / SQL / RAG / retrieval) | 53 |
| **With a recovered, re-runnable case** | **8** |
| **Still needing a case written by hand** | **45** |
| Recovered coverage | **15%** |

| The bank itself | Count |
|---|---|
| Total cases | 87 |
| Directly scorable (question + reference answer) | 79 |
| Deterministic retrieval cases (expected rows, no judge needed) | 6 |
| Provisional, flagged `needs_review` | 2 |
| Multi-turn follow-up links recovered | 10 |
| Distinct gaps referenced by any case | 13 |

**Why 8 and not 53, stated plainly:** the evidence directories are rich in questions and nearly empty of *gap attribution*. Only two places in the entire repo link a question to a gap number — the `Notes` column of the two `live_test_results.md` files (which cites a gap only on failing turns) and `tests/agent_eval_golden_sample.py`'s `why_on_file` field. That is a property of how the evidence was written, not of the parser. The 87 cases are real and useful — 79 gradeable questions where there were 9 — but they are organised **per tenant, not per gap**.

Two caveats that travel with these numbers: the 53 is a keyword classifier over hand-written tracker prose and slightly over-counts (it sweeps in a few non-chat gaps whose titles mention chat), and the four source question banks live in gitignored directories, so the fixture is derived from content not currently in version control.

Gap 287 — a faithfulness change that regressed Gap 263's already-fixed behaviour and was caught by a user rather than by a test — is one of the 45 with no case. It is the concrete cost of the distance between those two numbers.

### 8. Health — day over day

Alerts fired per day, from Feature 20's existing 25+ alert rules. No new alert rule is created by this feature.

content.query:
alertsmanagementresources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.alertsmanagement/alerts'
| extend fired = todatetime(properties.essentials.startDateTime),
         sev = tostring(properties.essentials.severity),
         state = tostring(properties.essentials.alertState),
         rule = tostring(properties.essentials.alertRule),
         target = tostring(properties.essentials.targetResourceName)
| where fired > ago({TimeRange:seconds}s)
| summarize alerts = count() by day = startofday(fired), sev
| order by day asc
content.title: Alerts fired per day, by severity

content.json:
### How to import this

Portal → Monitor → Workbooks → **New** → the `</>` (Advanced Editor) button → paste this file's
contents over the default template → **Apply** → **Save** (pick resource group `rg-invoice-llm-dev`).
Nothing in this repo deploys it; it is a definition, not a deployment.

**If a section renders empty**, read the honesty table at the top of this workbook before assuming a healthy zero. Sections 1-6 all depend on `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` being set as a Container App secret; sections 2 and 6 additionally depend on things that are not running yet (`ENABLE_AGENTIC_SAGE` for the `sage.*` events, and any job at all that calls `emit_online_signals()`).

**If the Health section shows "unsupported query type"** on import: that step is an Azure Resource
Graph query (`queryType: 1`). Re-pick *Azure Resource Graph* as the data source in edit mode and
paste the same query back — the query text itself is verified working against this subscription.

ARG was used rather than the built-in **Alerts** step type on purpose: the built-in step lists
alerts as they are *right now*, and this workbook's whole point is day-over-day trend on one shared
axis. `alertsmanagementresources` carries `startDateTime`, so alerts can be binned by day next to
the cost and quality series. Feature 20's 25+ alert rules and their action groups are unchanged —
nothing here creates or edits an alert rule.
